# eis-ds

> eis-ds is a visual design system in plain HTML and CSS: tokens (colour, type, space, shape), basic elements and scope components. A page links one CSS file and builds with native HTML and `eis-` classes. Light mode only.

This file is for LLMs and agents that build pages with eis-ds. Read the manual before you write HTML or CSS, and apply it literally. For the full manual in one file, read [llms-full.txt](https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/llms-full.txt). To match a pinned release, read the same file from the tag: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diegoeis/eis-ds/<tag>/llms-full.txt`.

Load one scope. Do not load a separate font link:

- Web scope (websites, landing pages, documentation): `https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/dist/eis-web.min.css`
- App scope (dashboards, tools, system screens): `https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/dist/eis-app.min.css`

Rules that have no exceptions:

- Use only the shared classes and the classes of your scope (`eis-web-*` or `eis-app-*`). Never mix scopes.
- Your own CSS holds layout only. Do not restyle an eis-ds element. Do not write CSS that eis-ds already covers.
- Use no raw values for colour, type, space or radius. Use the tokens. The manual lists the few allowed exceptions.
- Use semantic HTML and native controls: `table`, `button`, `a`, `input`, `select`, `details`, `fieldset`. Never make a control or a table from `div` or `span`.
- A variant changes colour only. A size (`--sm`, `--lg`) changes size only.
- A panel holds only its parts: `eis-panel__head`, `eis-panel__body` (the `id` of a script goes on it), an optional `eis-panel__footer`, or a full-width part the manual lists (table, list, disclosure, metrics). No wrapper between the panel and its parts. Never an `eis-panel__body` inside another one. The Save of a settings panel goes in its footer.
- Use the accent once per piece, on 5% of the area or less.
- Every piece works from 360px to wide screens, with no horizontal scroll.
- Before you finish, check the piece against the checklist.

## Manual

### Manual overview

Source: https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/docs/manual/AGENTS.md

#### eis-ds manual

The usage manual of the design system. Written to be applied literally by people and by LLMs: every rule is a "use / don't use", every element has HTML to copy.

Read these files in this order before you build anything:

| File | Answers |
|---|---|
| [`tokens-usage.md`](https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/docs/manual/tokens-usage.md) | Which variable do I use for this colour, size, space, radius or line? |
| [`elements.md`](https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/docs/manual/elements.md) | What HTML and classes make a button, chip, field, table, panel…? Which variant? |
| [`layout.md`](https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/docs/manual/layout.md) | How do I set up a page: files to load, page skeleton, grids, responsiveness, scopes (shared, web, app)? |
| [`checklist.md`](https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/docs/manual/checklist.md) | What must be true before a piece is done? |

Related, not part of the manual:

- `docs/tokens.md` — how tokens are **written** (W3C DTCG format). Read it only when adding or changing a token.
- `docs/visual-guidance/visual-guidance.md` — where the visual direction came from, and the decision log. Read it to understand *why*. This manual says *what*.
- `site/` (at the repository root) — the visual manual for humans: this manual applied and rendered. Start at `site/foundations.html`. The tokens and the CSS live in `src/`: `shared/`, `web/` and `app/` (see `layout.md` §7). When the manual and the CSS disagree, the CSS in `src/css/` wins. Then fix the manual.

For LLMs outside this repository, the site publishes the manual as one file: https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/llms-full.txt. `scripts/build-llms.py` generates it from this folder and `llms.txt`. A new file in this folder needs a link in `llms.txt`. The script also copies the section "Rules with no exceptions" below into `llms.txt`. Change the rules here, never in `llms.txt`.

##### Rules with no exceptions

The other files of this manual give the details of each rule.

- Use only the shared classes and the classes of your scope (`eis-web-*` or `eis-app-*`). Never mix scopes.
- Your own CSS holds layout only. Do not restyle an eis-ds element. Do not write CSS that eis-ds already covers.
- Use no raw values for colour, type, space or radius. Use the tokens. The manual lists the few allowed exceptions.
- Use semantic HTML and native controls: `table`, `button`, `a`, `input`, `select`, `details`, `fieldset`. Never make a control or a table from `div` or `span`.
- A variant changes colour only. A size (`--sm`, `--lg`) changes size only.
- A panel holds only its parts: `eis-panel__head`, `eis-panel__body` (the `id` of a script goes on it), an optional `eis-panel__footer`, or a full-width part the manual lists (table, list, disclosure, metrics). No wrapper between the panel and its parts. Never an `eis-panel__body` inside another one. The Save of a settings panel goes in its footer.
- Use the accent once per piece, on 5% of the area or less.
- Every piece works from 360px to wide screens, with no horizontal scroll.
- Before you finish, check the piece against the checklist.

##### Conventions used in this manual

- **MUST / MUST NOT** — no exceptions.
- **Prefer** — the default. Deviate only for a reason you can state.
- Code blocks are copy-ready. Replace only the text and the `id`/`for` values.
- This manual writes variable names without `var()`: `--ink` means `var(--ink)`.

---

### Tokens: usage

Source: https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/docs/manual/tokens-usage.md

#### Tokens: usage

Which variable to use for what. Shared variables come from `src/shared/css/tokens.css`. Scope variables (`--web-*`, `--app-*`) come from `src/<scope>/css/tokens.css`. All are generated — never edit them.

**Two layers.**
- **Semantic roles** (`--surface-*`, `--ink*`, `--line`, `--accent*`) carry meaning and will change between modes (dark, paper). For backgrounds, text, lines and the accent colour you **MUST** use the role, never the primitive behind it.
- **Primitives** (`--color-*`, `--space-*`, `--radius-*`, `--border-*`, `--font-*`): use them directly for everything that has no role: spacing, radii, type sizes and weights, and the grey ramp for data.

**No raw values.** You MUST NOT write a hex, rgb, px font size, px spacing or radius in piece CSS. If a value is missing, the token is missing: add it (see `docs/tokens.md`), don't hard-code it. [§8](#8-allowed-raw-values) lists the allowed exceptions.

---

##### 1. Colour roles

| Variable | Value | Use for | MUST NOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--surface-canvas` | `#f7f7f7` | Page background. Hover background of secondary/ghost controls. Background of an open disclosure summary. | Use as a card or panel background. |
| `--surface-raised` | `#ffffff` | Background of a default button: a control raised above the canvas. Same value as `--surface-panel` today, another role (see the note below the table). | Use for panels, cards or other page areas. It is not a third surface level. |
| `--surface-panel` | `#ffffff` | Panels, the app sidebar, inputs, table backgrounds: the surface that holds content. The second and **last** surface level. | Stack a panel inside a panel to get a third level. Use a line instead. |
| `--surface-inverse` | `#111111` | Primary and black buttons (`eis-button--primary`, `--black`), active nav item, solid chip. | Use for large areas. |
| `--line` | `#cfcfcf` | **Every** border, divider and hairline: panels, table rows, separators, chip outlines. | Use `--ink` or any darker grey for borders of shapes, panels or cards. |
| `--ink` | `#111111` | Primary text, headings, numbers, checked controls, focus outline. | — |
| `--ink-muted` | `#6d6d6d` | Secondary text, metadata, placeholders, **outlines of interactive controls** (input, checkbox, radio, switch). 5.2:1 on panel, 4.8:1 on canvas, 4.5:1 on selected. | Use for decorative borders (that is `--line`). Put on `--surface-hover` (4.3:1) or `--surface-head` (3.8:1): both fail. |
| `--ink-inverse` | `#f7f7f7` | Text on `--surface-inverse`. | Put on `--accent` (use `--accent-on`). |
| `--accent` | `#f35919` | **Fills and marks** for the one thing that matters: overdue, conflict, urgent, record. | Use as text on light surfaces (3.1:1, fails). Decorate. Exceed ~5% of the visible area. |
| `--accent-ink` | `#b5400c` | The accent **as text**: overdue dates, error messages, current breadcrumb item. 4.7:1 on canvas. | Use as a fill. |
| `--accent-on` | `#111111` | Text and icons placed **on** a `--accent` fill. 5.6:1. | Use white on `--accent` (3.1:1, fails). |
| `--success` | `#2a9d5c` | **Fills** for a positive state: done, saved, sent. Also the save button when the page needs one (`eis-button--success`). | Use as text on light surfaces (2.9:1, fails). Use it to decorate or to compete with the accent. |
| `--success-ink` | `#16753f` | Success **as text**: "Saved", "Sent". 4.8:1 on canvas. | Use as a fill. |
| `--success-on` | `#111111` | Text and icons **on** a `--success` fill. 5.5:1. | Use white on `--success` (3.5:1, fails). |
| `--danger` | `#e5484d` | **Fill** of a danger button on hover. | Use as text (use `--danger-ink`), or to decorate. |
| `--danger-ink` | `#b42318` | Danger **as text** and the line of a danger button. 6.6:1 on white. | Use as a fill. |
| `--danger-on` | `#111111` | Text **on** a `--danger` fill. 4.8:1. | Use white on `--danger` (3.9:1, fails). |
| `--surface-head` | `#dddddd` | Head strip of a panel. Text on it is `--ink` (13.9:1). `eis-mono` and an outline chip in the head take `--ink` by themselves. `eis-label` is always `--ink`. | Put `--ink-muted` on it (3.8:1, fails). Use as a page area. |
| `--surface-selected` | `#f0f0f0` | Background of a selected table row: the row has `aria-selected="true"`. `eis-table` sets it. Every text role passes on it (`--ink` 16.6:1, `--ink-muted` 4.5:1, `--accent-ink` 5.0:1). | Use as a page area, a panel or a hover. |
| `--surface-hover` | `#eaeaea` | Background of a closed disclosure summary under the pointer. `eis-disclosure` sets it. Text on it is `--ink` (15.7:1): `eis-mono` in the summary takes `--ink` on hover by itself. `eis-label` is always `--ink`. `--accent-ink` passes (4.7:1). | Put `--ink-muted` on it (4.3:1, fails). Use as a page area or a selected state. |

**`--surface-panel` and `--surface-raised` have the same value today (white), with two roles.** `--surface-panel` is a surface that holds content (panel, sidebar, field, table). `--surface-raised` is a control raised above the canvas (the default button). Keep both: a mode (dark, paper) can give them different values. Use the role of the job, never the one with the right colour.

###### Accent budget

- One accent per piece. If two things compete for it, one of them is not important.
- Small state marks do not count for this rule: a count badge (`eis-app-nav__count--accent`), an overdue dot, a due date in `--accent-ink`. They can be on the same piece as the one accent action.
- Accent covers ≤ 5% of the area. Exception: one "accent block" (a whole section in `--accent`) per page, declared on purpose.
- Normal data is grey. Accent marks only the exception.

###### Pairing quick-reference

| Background | Text | Secondary text | Accent text |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--surface-canvas` | `--ink` | `--ink-muted` | `--accent-ink` |
| `--surface-panel` | `--ink` | `--ink-muted` | `--accent-ink` |
| `--surface-selected` | `--ink` | `--ink-muted` | `--accent-ink` |
| `--surface-hover` | `--ink` | — (use `--ink`) | `--accent-ink` |
| `--surface-inverse` | `--ink-inverse` | — | — |
| `--accent` | `--accent-on` | — | — |
| `--success` | `--success-on` | — | — |

Any other pair MUST be measured (WCAG 2.1: 4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text and UI graphics) before use.

##### 2. Neutral primitives

Use the role above whenever one exists. Use these primitives directly **only** for data visualisation and the cases listed.

| Variable | Value | Direct use allowed for |
|---|---|---|
| `--color-white` | `#ffffff` | — (use `--surface-panel` / `--surface-raised`) |
| `--color-neutral-0` | `#f7f7f7` | — (use `--surface-canvas` / `--ink-inverse`) |
| `--color-neutral-50` | `#f0f0f0` | — (use `--surface-selected`) |
| `--color-neutral-100` | `#eaeaea` | — (use `--surface-hover`) |
| `--color-neutral-200` | `#dddddd` | Data ramp, lowest step. |
| `--color-neutral-300` | `#cfcfcf` | Data ramp. (As a border, use `--line`.) |
| `--color-neutral-400` | `#a3a3a3` | Data ramp. |
| `--color-neutral-500` | `#858585` | Data ramp. Icons and non-text graphics (3.4:1 on panel). Section labels in the app sidebar (`.eis-app-sidebar .eis-label`, author's choice). Never body text. |
| `--color-neutral-600` | `#6d6d6d` | Data ramp. (As text, use `--ink-muted`.) |
| `--color-neutral-900` | `#111111` | Data ramp, highest step. (As text, use `--ink`.) |

###### Data ramp

Ordinal data (age, volume, intensity) goes from light to dark, low to high:

`--color-neutral-200` → `300` → `400` → `500` → `600` → `900`, and `--accent` for the exception (overdue, anomaly).

- Use as many steps as there are buckets, keeping the order. With fewer than 6 buckets, prefer skipping steps so neighbours differ more (e.g. 4 buckets: `200 · 400 · 600 · 900`).
- `200` and `300` are close (1.15:1). Don't put them next to each other when the difference matters.
- No hues for data. Status colours: `--success` (green) for a positive state, `--danger` (red) only on a remove/delete button. The accent still marks problems.

###### Category colours

Seven hues tell groups apart: a team, a project, a topic, a calendar type. They are not data values and not states. Use them directly, as primitives.

| Variable | Value | `--ink` on it | Pastel tone | `--ink` on pastel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--color-pink` | `#ff6a8c` | 6.9:1 | `#ffb4c6` | 11.3:1 |
| `--color-terracotta` | `#e8906e` | 7.8:1 | `#f4c8b6` | 12.4:1 |
| `--color-yellow` | `#ffd966` | 13.8:1 | `#ffecb2` | 16.1:1 |
| `--color-green` | `#98d9a4` | 11.5:1 | `#ccecd2` | 14.8:1 |
| `--color-aqua` | `#7fcfd0` | 10.6:1 | `#bfe7e8` | 14.2:1 |
| `--color-blue` | `#9db4ff` | 9.4:1 | `#cedaff` | 13.6:1 |
| `--color-lilac` | `#c3a6f2` | 9.0:1 | `#e1d2f8` | 13.3:1 |
| `--color-pastel` | `0.5` | — | — | — |

- The pastel tone is not a token. Mix the hue with white at `--color-pastel`:
  `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-blue) calc(var(--color-pastel) * 100%), var(--color-white))`. On a chip, add `eis-chip--pastel` instead.
- `--color-green` is the green category. `--color-green-500` and `--color-green-700` are the success colours. Do not use one for the other.
- Text and icons on a category colour are `--ink`. `--ink-muted` fails on some of them (1.9:1 on pink). White fails on all of them.
- Use: chip fills, tag and legend dots, calendar events, illustration.
- Do not use: as text, as a page or panel surface, for a state (use `--accent`, `--success`, `--danger`), for ordinal data (use the data ramp).
- The fills are light. They do not reach 3:1 against the canvas (pastel yellow is 1.1:1). The text inside carries the meaning, so this is correct for a chip. A shape with no text in a category colour needs a `--line` border.

##### 3. Space

Seven steps, each double the previous. Each has a job. Pick by job, not by eye.

| Variable | Value | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `--space-100` | 8px | **Inside a component**: icon ↔ label, gap between chips, label ↔ field, field ↔ hint. |
| `--space-200` | 16px | **Between siblings**: panel padding, table cell padding, list rows, gap between panels in a grid. |
| `--space-300` | 32px | **Between blocks**: page padding (desktop), gap between page regions, title ↔ content of a section. |
| `--space-400` | 64px | **Between sections**: large section gaps on documentation and marketing pages. |
| `--space-500` | 128px | **Large layout**: space around a hero or a page opening. |
| `--space-600` | 256px | **Large layout**: offsets on wide marketing pages. |
| `--space-700` | 512px | **Large layout**: the largest offset on wide marketing pages. |

- Use the half step `calc(--space-100 / 2)` (4px) only in dense data: cell grids, tabs padding, list item gaps.
- Mobile page padding drops one step (`--space-300` → `--space-200`).
- Use `--space-500` to `--space-700` only in page layout on wide screens. Never use them inside a component. Below 1024px, drop them to `--space-400` or less.

###### Width

Five fixed widths for a field or a block, used through the width helpers (`eis-width-100` … `eis-width-500`, `eis-width-fit` for "as wide as the content"; see elements.md, "Labels and helpers"). Pick the smallest that fits the longest value the field holds. In a row of fields (`eis-app-add-bar`, `eis-app-form-row`, `eis-app-filters__fields`) the step is the base and the minimum width of the field: it grows into the free room, and wraps when it no longer fits (layout.md §7, "Rows of fields").

| Variable | Value | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `--width-100` | 128px | A short value: a number, a date, a status select |
| `--width-200` | 192px | A word or two: a type, a name |
| `--width-300` | 256px | A short line: a title, an e-mail |
| `--width-400` | 360px | A path, a URL |
| `--width-500` | 480px | A long line |

##### 4. Radius and line

| Variable | Value | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `--radius-100` | 7px | Buttons, inputs, selects, tabs, nav items, small boxes. |
| `--radius-200` | 10px | Panels. |
| `--radius-300` | 15px | Large surfaces: a card that stands alone, a dialog. |
| `--radius-400` | 20px | The largest surfaces: sheets, hero blocks. |
| `--radius-full` | 999px | Chips, switch, avatar, pills. |

Nested corners: an element inside a rounded box with padding uses the box radius minus the padding, so the curves stay parallel.
| `--border-width-100` | 1px | **The only line weight.** Every border and divider. |

- Only the focus outline uses 2px.
- No shadows. The only exception is the button hover glow (defined in `elements.css`), never at rest.

##### 5. Type

Two voices. **Sans** (`--font-family-sans`, Geist) speaks text. **Mono** (`--font-family-mono`, Geist Mono) speaks for the instrument: labels, numbers, dates, codes, sources, navigation, buttons.

###### Text styles — prefer these

Apply with the class (`.eis-type-*`) or the per-property variables (`--type-<style>-font-size`, `-font-family`, `-font-weight`, `-letter-spacing`, `-line-height`).

| Style | Spec | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `display` | sans 56 / 300 / −1.5 / 1 | Page title (`h1`). One per page. Use `clamp(--font-size-600, 5vw, --font-size-800)` for responsiveness. |
| `heading` | sans 24 / 400 / 1.25 | Section titles in documents and pages. |
| `lead` | sans 18 / 400 / 1.45 | Intro paragraph under a title. |
| `body` | sans 14 / 400 / 1.45 | Body text, UI text, task text, table text. The default on `<body>`. |
| `metric` | mono 48 / 300 / −1.5 / 1 | Big numbers in panels and summaries. `--font-size-600` on mobile. |
| `mono` | mono 12 / 400 | Dates, times, sources, metadata, counts, codes. Also `.eis-mono`. |
| `label` | mono 11 / 500 / +0.88 / UPPERCASE | Panel titles, table headers, field labels, nav section titles. Also `.eis-label`. |

Rules:
- Numbers that line up (tables, metrics, counts) MUST be mono with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (`.eis-mono` and `.eis-num` already do it).
- UPPERCASE is only for `label` style and buttons. Running text MUST be sentence case.
- Weights: 300 for display/metric, 400 for text, 500 for labels and emphasis, 600 only for the brand mark. No bold (700).
- Don't invent sizes. Use `--font-size-100…800`.

##### 6. Mode

Only the light mode exists. Pieces MUST still use roles for surfaces/ink/line/accent so a dark mode can be added by redefining roles only.

##### 7. Scope tokens

Use a scope token only inside that scope.

| Variable | Value | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `--web-size-sheet` | 1440px | Max width of the landing sheet. |
| `--web-size-page` | 1280px | Max width of a documentation page. |
| `--web-font-size-hero` | 134px | Hero title. Use `clamp(--font-size-700, 9vw, --web-font-size-hero)`. |
| `--web-font-size-cta` | 100px | Closing call-to-action title. |
| `--web-font-size-section` | = `--font-size-800` | Landing section titles. |
| `--web-font-size-sub` | 16px | Hero sub-paragraph (`eis-web-hero__sub`). |
| `--web-font-size-specimen` | 90px | Large type specimen. |
| `--app-size-sidebar` | 248px | Sidebar width. |
| `--app-size-sidebar-collapsed` | 64px | Collapsed sidebar width: the toggle plus the side padding. |
| `--app-size-main` | 1200px | Max width of the main content, without its padding. |
| `--app-size-aside` | 360px | Side column width. |
| `--app-size-nav-item` | 32px | Min height of a navigation item. |
| `--app-size-row` | 44px | Min height of a list row. |
| `--app-size-avatar` | 28px | Avatar size in lists. |
| `--app-size-filter-field` | 192px | Width of a labelled field in a filter bar (`eis-app-filters`). |
| `--app-size-filter-search` | 224px | Width of the search field in a filter bar. |
| `--app-size-form-field` | 256px | Min width of a column in a form row (`eis-app-form-row`). Columns wrap below it. |

##### 8. Allowed raw values

The only places a literal number is acceptable in piece CSS:
- Component dimensions: control heights (40px, 24px chips), icon and avatar sizes, checkbox 16px, fixed sidebar width, column widths in a table.
- `calc(--space-100 / 2)` in dense data.
- `0`, `100%`, `1fr`, `auto`, percentages and viewport/container units in layout.
- Breakpoints in `@media`.
- Opacity `.4` for disabled.

---

### Elements

Source: https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/docs/manual/elements.md

#### Elements

Every basic element: when to use it, the HTML to copy, variants, and what is forbidden. Styles live in `src/shared/css/elements.css`. Elements are shared by every scope. The rendered versions are on `site/elements.html`.

**General rules for all elements**

- MUST use the native HTML element that carries the meaning. A `div` or `span` never pretends to be a button, checkbox, table, list or form.
- Every class starts with `eis-`. Naming: block `eis-panel`, part `eis-panel__head`, variant `eis-chip--accent`, state `eis-is-accent`.
- A **variant changes colour only** (through the local `--bg`, `--fg`, `--bd`, `--glow`). Never size, padding, radius, structure or behaviour.
- A **size** (`--sm`, `--lg`) changes size only: height, padding, gap and font size, all from the spacing and type tokens. Never colour. Combine one size with any variant. No size class = medium.
- A piece MUST NOT restyle an element from `elements.css`. If it needs something different, change the element in the system (and on `elements.html`).
- Every control is keyboard-reachable and has a visible focus (`:focus-visible`, 2px `--ink` outline — already global).

---

##### Decision table: which element?

| You need to… | Use |
|---|---|
| Trigger an action (save, filter, export, create) | **Button** `<button class="eis-button">` |
| Go to another page | **Link** `<a>` — styled as button (`<a class="eis-button">`) only if it's a call to action |
| Show a status, category, tag, code, count | **Chip** `<span class="eis-chip">` |
| Pick several independent options | **Checkbox** |
| Pick one of a few options in a form | **Radio** group |
| Pick one of many options | **Select** |
| Pick several of many options, and show the picks in the field | **Multi-select** `<div class="eis-multiselect">` |
| Turn a setting on/off that applies immediately | **Switch** |
| Switch the view of the current page (Today / Week / All) | **Tabs** |
| Show items one per row, with a short text and an action or status | **List** `<ul class="eis-list">` |
| Group each part of a panel body that has two or more titled parts | **Panel section** `<section class="eis-panel__section">` |
| Split two parts of the same panel body that have no title | **Divider** `<hr>` |
| Show rows × columns of data | **Table** |
| Group content in a container | **Panel** |
| Group the buttons that end a form or a step, at the right | **Actions** `<div class="eis-actions">` |
| Content that opens and closes | **Disclosure** (`<details>`) |
| Label–value pairs (metrics, metadata) | `<dl>`. A row of numbers: **Metrics** `<dl class="eis-metrics">` |

**Button vs chip** — the most common mistake:

| | Button | Chip |
|---|---|---|
| Meaning | Acts | Describes |
| Shape | Rectangle, `--radius-100` | Pill, `--radius-full` |
| Text | MONO UPPERCASE, tracked | Mono sentence case |
| Height | 40px | 24px |
| Cursor | pointer | default |
| Hover | Background change + glow | None |
| Element | `<button>` / `<a>` | `<span>` |

A status MUST be a chip. A chip MUST NOT be clickable.

Naming: the orange is **accent** (`--accent`, `eis-button--accent`, `eis-chip--accent`), the market name for the brand highlight colour. The main action is **primary** (`eis-button--primary`, ink fill). `eis-button--black` is the same ink fill as a colour, for a dark button that is not the main action (a pressed choice). A remove or delete action is **danger** (`eis-button--danger`). Plain `eis-button` is the default (white).

---

##### Button

```html
<button class="eis-button eis-button--primary" type="button">Save</button>
<button class="eis-button" type="button">Cancel</button>
<button class="eis-button eis-button--ghost" type="button">Skip</button>
<button class="eis-button eis-button--accent" type="button">Record</button>
<button class="eis-button" type="button" disabled>Disabled</button>
```

| Variant | Use for | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `--primary` | The main action of a view, or of a panel that saves on its own (each Save on a settings page). | Use for a secondary action. |
| `--black` | Ink fill as a colour: a pressed choice, a dark button that is not the main action. | Use for the main action (use `--primary`). |
| `--danger` | Remove, delete: an action that loses data. A ghost with a red line and red text (`--danger-ink`); on hover it fills `--danger` with dark text. | Use for anything that does not remove or break. |
| *(default)* | Secondary actions. White background (`--surface-raised`), line border. | — |
| `--ghost` | Low-emphasis actions next to others (Skip, Clear). | No glow on hover. |
| `--accent` | Only when the action **is** the accent: record, go live, publish. In the app scope: the main action of the page head (`eis-app-page-head`), e.g. "New task" (layout.md §7, "Page head"). | Rare: one per page, and it counts toward the accent budget. Never "Save" or "Delete". |
| `--success` | Save, when the page asks for a positive action in green. | Not together with a `--primary` button for the same action. |

- `type="button"` unless it submits a form (`type="submit"`) or resets (`type="reset"`).
- Hover: background shifts and a glow in the variant's colour appears (built in). Don't add your own shadow.
- Disabled: the `disabled` attribute, never a class.
- Order in a group: secondary/ghost first, the `--primary` button last (rightmost).

###### Button with an icon

```html
<button class="eis-button eis-button--primary" type="button"><i data-lucide="plus" class="eis-icon"></i>New topic</button>
<a class="eis-button" href="/report">Open report<i data-lucide="arrow-right" class="eis-icon"></i></a>
<button class="eis-button eis-button--icon eis-button--sm" type="button" aria-label="Edit topic" title="Edit topic"><i data-lucide="pencil" class="eis-icon"></i></button>
```

- The icon goes before the text (left) or after it (right). The button gap spaces it. Left is the default. Use right only for a direction: next, open, external.
- `eis-button--icon`: a square button with only an icon. It MUST have `aria-label` and `title` with the action. Combine it with any variant and size. Use it for repeated actions in a row or a table (edit, remove, archive), where a text button does not fit.
- One icon per button. Never an icon only for decoration in a text button that is clear without it.
- Never type a character as an icon (`+`, `→`, `×`, `✓`). Use the Lucide icon.

| Size | Height | Padding | Font | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--sm` | `--space-300` (32px) | 1.5 × `--space-100` | `--font-size-100` | Actions inside a row, a table or a dense toolbar. |
| *(default)* | 40px | `--space-200` | `--font-size-200` | Forms and page toolbars. |
| `--lg` | 1.5 × `--space-300` (48px) | `--space-300` | `--font-size-300` | The single main action of an empty state or landing view. |

##### Chip

```html
<span class="eis-chip">Accepted</span>
<span class="eis-chip eis-chip--outline">PLT-204</span>
<span class="eis-chip eis-chip--solid">Organizer</span>
<span class="eis-chip eis-chip--accent">Overdue</span>
<span class="eis-chip eis-chip--hatch">Cancelled</span>
<span class="eis-chip eis-chip--dot">On track</span>
<span class="eis-chip eis-chip--blue">Platform</span>
<span class="eis-chip eis-chip--blue eis-chip--pastel">Platform</span>
```

| Variant | Use for |
|---|---|
| *(default)* | Neutral status: accepted, waiting, on track. |
| `--outline` | Identifiers and categories: ticket codes, stream names. |
| `--solid` | Strong neutral status: new, organizer, problem. |
| `--accent` | The exception: overdue, conflict, urgent. Counts toward the accent budget. |
| `--success` | A positive state: done, sent, saved. |
| `--hatch` | What no longer counts: cancelled, blocked. |
| `--dot` | Adds a status dot. Combine it with any variant. |
| `--pink`, `--terracotta`, `--yellow`, `--green`, `--aqua`, `--blue`, `--lilac` | Categories: a team, a project, a topic, a calendar type. The colour tells groups apart. It does not mark a state. |
| `--pastel` | The light tone of the same hue. Put it after a category colour: `eis-chip eis-chip--blue eis-chip--pastel`. It has no effect on other variants. |

| Size | Height | Padding | Font | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--sm` | `--space-200` (16px) | 0.75 × `--space-100` | `--font-size-100` | Inline with a line of text: a task title, a table cell. |
| *(default)* | 24px | 10px | `--font-size-200` | Meta rows, lists, panel heads. |
| `--lg` | `--space-300` (32px) | 1.5 × `--space-100` | `--font-size-300` | A status that leads a section or a page head. |

- Text in sentence case (`Overdue`, not `OVERDUE`).
- Never wrap a chip in `<a>` or `<button>`.
- A chip that shows a value the user picked can hold one remove button, `<button class="eis-chip__remove">`, after its text. The CSS draws the Lucide `x`. Give the button `aria-label` and `title` ("Remove Billing"). Only the button reacts to the pointer. The chip stays without hover. The multi-select writes these chips for you.
- Give each category one colour, and keep it in all views. Use one tone per set: all mid tone or all pastel. Use the mid tone when the chips must stand out, and the pastel tone in dense lists.
- Never use a category colour for a state. Overdue is `--accent`, done is `--success`.
- With more than seven categories, use `--outline` for the rest. Do not repeat a colour in one view.

##### Fields

```html
<div class="eis-field">
  <label for="title">Title</label>
  <input class="eis-input" id="title" name="title" type="text" placeholder="What needs to be done" aria-describedby="title-hint">
  <p class="eis-field__hint" id="title-hint">Start with a verb.</p>
</div>

<div class="eis-field">
  <label for="stream">Stream</label>
  <select class="eis-select" id="stream" name="stream">
    <option>Priority</option><option>Billing</option>
  </select>
</div>

<div class="eis-field">
  <label for="owner">Owner</label>
  <input class="eis-input" id="owner" name="owner" type="email" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="owner-err">
  <p class="eis-field__error" id="owner-err">Enter a valid email.</p>
</div>

<div class="eis-field">
  <label for="notes">Notes</label>
  <textarea class="eis-textarea" id="notes" name="notes"></textarea>
</div>
```

- Label always above the control, always present, linked with `for`/`id`. A placeholder is not a label.
- A fieldset field (a group of options, a multi-select) uses `<legend>` as its label. The legend has the same style and the same gap to the control as a label.
- Use the right `type`: `email`, `date`, `number`, `search`, `url`…
- Error: `aria-invalid="true"` on the control + `aria-describedby` pointing to `.eis-field__error`. Never colour alone.
- Hint and error sit below the control. An empty hint or error takes no room, so a script can keep the `<p>` and fill it on demand.
- Fields always use body type, also inside a label-styled container (a panel title being edited).
- Put fields in a `<form>`. Put the actions at the end, the `--primary` button last.

###### Multi-select

```html
<fieldset class="eis-field">
  <legend>Teams</legend>
  <div class="eis-multiselect" data-eis-multiselect>
    <ul class="eis-multiselect__chips" aria-label="Selected teams"></ul>
    <details class="eis-multiselect__menu">
      <summary><span class="eis-multiselect__placeholder">Select teams</span></summary>
      <div class="eis-multiselect__options">
        <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-checkbox" type="checkbox" name="teams" value="billing" checked> Billing</label>
        <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-checkbox" type="checkbox" name="teams" value="platform"> Platform</label>
        <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-checkbox" type="checkbox" name="teams" value="data"> Data</label>
      </div>
    </details>
  </div>
</fieldset>
```

Load the script at the end of `<body>`:

```html
<script src="<src>/shared/js/multiselect.js"></script>
```

The script starts the fields that are in the page when it loads. A page that adds a field later (from a template) calls `EisMultiselect.init(container)` after it adds the field. The call starts each field in `container`, or `container` itself. A field that already runs is not started again.

- Use it to pick several values from a list of about 5 to 30 options: teams, tags, people. The picks stay visible in the field. For 2 to 4 options, show the checkboxes in a `fieldset` (see "Checkbox, radio, switch"). To pick one value, use the select.
- The options are native checkboxes in a `<details>`. The form sends the checked values with or without the script. Give every checkbox the same `name`.
- The field is a `fieldset` with a `legend`, because it holds a group of controls.
- `shared/js/multiselect.js` shows each checked option as a chip with a remove button (`eis-chip__remove`), in the order of the list. The remove button unchecks the option. Esc and a click outside the field close the list. After a remove, the focus goes to the next remove button, or to the summary.
- The placeholder in `__placeholder` shows while the user has no option checked. With a value, it leaves the view, but screen readers still read it as the name of the summary.
- The list stays open while the user checks options. It is as wide as the field, and scrolls when it is taller than 256px (2 × `--space-500`).
- The field grows in height when the chips wrap to more rows. With no value, or with chips on one row, it is 40px tall, as the other fields.
- A script that checks an option from code must dispatch a `change` event (`bubbles: true`) on the checkbox, so the chips follow. A form reset updates the chips.
- Error: put `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` on the `fieldset`, and the `.eis-field__error` after the `.eis-multiselect`.

###### Form

```html
<form class="eis-panel eis-form" action="/tasks" method="post">
  <div class="eis-field">
    <label for="title">Title</label>
    <input class="eis-input" id="title" name="title" type="text">
  </div>
  <div class="eis-field">
    <label for="due">Due</label>
    <input class="eis-input" id="due" name="due" type="date">
  </div>
  <div class="eis-field eis-field--wide">
    <label for="notes">Notes</label>
    <textarea class="eis-textarea" id="notes" name="notes"></textarea>
  </div>
  <div class="eis-actions">
    <button class="eis-button eis-button--ghost" type="reset">Clear</button>
    <button class="eis-button eis-button--primary" type="submit">Create task</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

- `.eis-form` goes on the `<form>`. It sets the fields in two equal columns, with its own padding. Put it on the same element as `eis-panel`: the form is the panel.
- `.eis-field--wide` makes a field take the whole row: a textarea, a long text. It works only inside `.eis-form`.
- Close the form with an `.eis-actions` as the last child (see "Actions"). In `.eis-form` it takes the whole row.
- At ≤640px the form has one column.
- Use it for a form that is the whole content of a panel (create, edit). Don't use it for fields in an `eis-panel__body` next to other content.
- In the app scope, a settings panel lays out its fields with `eis-app-form-row` inside `eis-panel__body`, and its buttons in `eis-panel__footer` (layout.md §7). Don't mix `eis-form` with `eis-app-form-row`.

###### Actions

```html
<div class="eis-actions">
  <button class="eis-button eis-button--ghost" type="button">Cancel</button>
  <button class="eis-button eis-button--primary" type="submit">Create task</button>
</div>
```

- `.eis-actions` groups the buttons of one task: Cancel and Create, Clear and Save. It puts them at the right, in one row that wraps, with a `--line` above it.
- The `--primary` button goes last. Use one `--primary` button in a group, or none.
- Use it in an `eis-form` (as the last child), at the end of an `eis-panel__body`, or in a page section with no panel. It is not a panel part: never put it as a direct child of an `eis-panel`.
- Use `<button>` elements, or `<a class="eis-button">` for a link. A group holds only buttons.
- `eis-actions` vs `eis-panel__footer`: the footer is the bottom part of a panel. It has no line above it and acts on the whole panel. The Save of a settings panel stays in `eis-panel__footer` (see "Panel structure"). Use `eis-actions` for a group of buttons inside content: the end of a form, or a step in a body.

##### Checkbox, radio, switch

```html
<fieldset class="eis-field">
  <legend>Show</legend>
  <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-checkbox" type="checkbox" checked> Overdue</label>
  <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-checkbox" type="checkbox"> New today</label>
</fieldset>

<fieldset class="eis-field">
  <legend>Sort by</legend>
  <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-radio" type="radio" name="sort" checked> Due date</label>
  <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-radio" type="radio" name="sort"> Age</label>
</fieldset>

<label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-switch" type="checkbox" role="switch"> Compact rows</label>
```

- Always use a real `<input>`. Restyle it with `appearance:none`. Never replace it with a `span`.
- Groups of related options go in `<fieldset class="eis-field">` + `<legend>`. On a `fieldset`, `eis-field` removes the border and stacks the options. No other class is necessary.
- Radios in one group share `name`.
- Switch = checkbox + `role="switch"`, only for settings that apply immediately (no Save button).
- Wrapping the input in `<label class="eis-choice">` makes the whole text clickable and gives the hover.
- In a table, a checkbox without visible text needs `aria-label` or a `<label for>`.

##### Tabs

```html
<fieldset class="eis-tabs">
  <legend>Range</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="range" value="today" checked><span>Today</span></label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="range" value="week"><span>Week</span></label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="range" value="all"><span>All</span></label>
</fieldset>
```

- It is a radio group (not ARIA tabs). Use it to switch the **view** of the current page, 2–4 options.
- The checked option has the `--surface-inverse` fill and `--ink-inverse` text, as the current item of a nav. An option under the pointer has the `--surface-canvas` fill.
- Height 40px, like the default button, input and select: in a toolbar, put tabs next to a default-size button (not `--sm`), and they line up.
- When the options do not fit the width (narrow screens), they wrap to more rows and each row fills the width. There is never a horizontal scroll.
- Radius `--radius-100`, like buttons, inputs and selects. The selected item uses the inner radius (`--radius-100` minus the padding).
- Not for navigation between pages (use links) and not for form answers (use radio).
- Count: when an option filters a list, put the number of items after its text, in `<span class="eis-tabs__count">` inside the option's `<span>`: `<span>Team <span class="eis-tabs__count">04</span></span>`. Two digits at least, as in metrics. The count of the whole list goes on `All`.

##### Table

```html
<div class="eis-panel">
  <table class="eis-table">
    <caption class="eis-visually-hidden">Open tasks by stream</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th scope="col"><span class="eis-visually-hidden">Select</span></th>
        <th scope="col">Stream</th>
        <th scope="col">Status</th>
        <th scope="col" class="eis-num">Open</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td><input class="eis-checkbox" type="checkbox" aria-label="Select Billing"></td>
        <th scope="row">Billing</th>
        <td><span class="eis-chip eis-chip--accent">Overdue</span></td>
        <td class="eis-num">13</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

- Tabular data MUST be `<table>` with `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<th scope>`. Never a grid of `div`s.
- Every table has a `<caption>` (visually hidden if the panel already has a title).
- Cells are vertically centred (`th`, `td`: `vertical-align: middle`). Don't override. A row that holds an `eis-disclosure` (a list that opens) aligns its cells to the top instead, so the row's title stays at the top when the list is open, and a disclosure after other content in the cell (a date, a text) keeps `--space-200` above it. The table sets both: write no class.
- Numbers: `.eis-num` (mono, tabular, right-aligned), including the header cell.
- Header row (`thead th`): `--surface-inverse` background, `--ink-inverse` text, label type, inner padding. A scope may change the inline padding of the header to align it with its cells. It never changes the colours.
- Rows separated by `--line`. No zebra stripes, no vertical lines.
- A selected row gets the `--surface-selected` background. A row is selected when it has `aria-selected="true"`; a checked checkbox in the row does not select it (a done task is not a selection). Write no class. Every text role passes on it, `--ink-muted` included.
- On narrow screens a table MAY reflow into cards with CSS (`display:block/grid` on `tr`), keeping the HTML a table. If it can't reflow, wrap it in a horizontally scrollable container — the page itself MUST NOT scroll sideways.

##### Panel

```html
<section class="eis-panel" aria-labelledby="agenda-h">
  <header class="eis-panel__head">
    <h2 class="eis-panel__title" id="agenda-h">Today's agenda</h2>
    <span class="eis-mono">10:30 — 17:15</span>
  </header>
  <!-- content -->
</section>
```

- The only container. `--surface-panel`, 1px `--line`, `--radius-100`, no shadow.
- Head: `--surface-head` background, text in `--ink`. The title is `eis-panel__title` (label type, ink: it names the panel, it is not a muted label) on the left, mono meta (count, range) on the right. `eis-mono` and an outline chip in the head take `--ink`: `--ink-muted` fails on `--surface-head` (3.8:1). `eis-label` is in `--ink` on every surface.
- MUST NOT nest a panel inside a panel. Separate inside with hairlines.
- Content padding: `--space-200`.

###### Panel structure

A panel holds only its parts, as direct children, in this order:

```html
<section class="eis-panel" aria-labelledby="run-h">
  <header class="eis-panel__head"><h2 class="eis-panel__title" id="run-h">Run</h2></header>
  <div class="eis-panel__body" id="run"><!-- fields, text. The id of a script goes here --></div>
  <footer class="eis-panel__footer"><button class="eis-button eis-button--primary" type="button">Save</button></footer>
</section>
```

- The head is first. Use it when the panel has a title. The footer is last and optional. A panel has one head and one footer at most.
- MUST NOT put a wrapper (`div`, `form`, `section`) between the panel and its parts. Loose content (a heading, a paragraph, a field, a button) goes in the body, never directly in the panel.
- In place of a body, a panel can hold a full-width element that has its own padding: `eis-table` (or the horizontal scroll wrapper of a table that can't reflow), `eis-list`, `eis-disclosure`, `eis-metrics`, or a scope component that `layout.md` §7 lists as a panel part. Put it directly in the panel, after the head.
- The panel can be the content itself: a list (`<ul class="eis-panel eis-list">`) or a form with no title (`<form class="eis-panel eis-form">`, see Form). Its children are then the rows or the fields. It has no head, body or footer.
- MUST NOT put an `eis-panel__body` inside another `eis-panel__body` or inside an `eis-panel__section`. A `<form>` inside a body gets no `eis-panel__body` class.
- A panel with a head and a footer that submits a form: make the `<form>` the panel (`<form class="eis-panel">`, with the head, the body and the footer in it). The `<form>` never sits between the panel and its parts.
- The Save button of a settings panel (it saves the whole panel) goes in `eis-panel__footer`, never in the body or the head. A button that acts on one row or one field (Save of one key, Remove) stays in that row.
- In an `eis-disclosure`, the same parts come after the `<summary>`: a body, then an optional footer.
- `scripts/check-css.py` fails when a page in `site/` or `index.html` breaks these rules.

- `eis-panel__body`: the padded content area under the head. Its children stack with a `--space-200` gap. Use it for any panel that holds fields or text, not for a panel that holds a table or a metric row.
- When a script fills the body of a panel, put the `id` on the body itself: `<div class="eis-panel__body" id="doctor">`. The script writes the content into it. Never put an empty `<div id="…">` in the panel, or around or inside the body, for the script: the body loses its padding and gap, or the content gets them twice. The same rule applies to an `eis-panel__section` that a script fills.
- `eis-bleed` (helper): a direct child of `eis-panel__body` that touches the panel edges: no side padding, none above it when it is first, none below it when it is last. Use it for a quoted block or a strip, never to remove the body padding of fields.
- `eis-panel__footer`: the bottom area for actions. Same padding, buttons in one row that wraps. No line above it. After a body it drops its top padding, so body and footer share one gap.

###### Panel section

```html
<section class="eis-panel" aria-labelledby="ws-h">
  <header class="eis-panel__head"><h2 class="eis-panel__title" id="ws-h">Workspace</h2></header>
  <div class="eis-panel__body">
    <section class="eis-panel__section" aria-labelledby="ws-daily-h">
      <h3 class="eis-label" id="ws-daily-h">Daily notes folder</h3>
      <div class="eis-field">
        <label for="ws-daily">Folder</label>
        <input class="eis-input" id="ws-daily" type="text" value="notes/daily">
      </div>
    </section>
    <section class="eis-panel__section" aria-labelledby="ws-topics-h">
      <h3 class="eis-label" id="ws-topics-h">Your topics</h3>
      <p>Topics that only this workspace uses.</p>
      <p><button class="eis-button eis-button--sm" type="button"><i data-lucide="plus" class="eis-icon"></i>Topic</button></p>
      <ul class="eis-list eis-bleed">…</ul>
    </section>
  </div>
  <footer class="eis-panel__footer"><button class="eis-button eis-button--primary" type="button">Save</button></footer>
</section>
```

- Use `eis-panel__section` when a panel body has two or more parts, and each part has a title. Put one section around each whole part: its title and all its content (text, fields, buttons, a list).
- When the body has only one part, do not use a section. Put the content directly in `eis-panel__body`. The panel title names it.
- A section is a direct child of `eis-panel__body`. Do not mix sections and loose content in one body. Do not put a section in a section.
- The title is the first child: `<h3 class="eis-label">` with an `id` (one level below the panel title). The `<section>` has `aria-labelledby` with that `id`. The section shows its title one step up (`--font-size-200`), as the heading of a disclosure, so it reads above the field labels of the part.
- The content of a section stacks with a `--space-200` gap, as in the body. `eis-bleed` works in a section as it does in the body.
- From the second section on, a `--line` above the section touches the panel edges. Do not write an `<hr>` between sections.

##### Disclosure

```html
<details class="eis-disclosure" open>
  <summary><h3>Payments</h3><span class="eis-mono">13</span></summary>
  <!-- content -->
</details>
```

- Native `<details>`/`<summary>`. It opens and closes without JS. It is the only element that opens and closes: groups of tasks, topics or any list use it too.
- The CSS draws the marker on the right: Lucide `plus` when closed, `minus` when open. Write no icon in the summary. When open, the summary gets `--surface-canvas` background and a `--line` under it. A closed summary under the pointer gets `--surface-hover`; `eis-mono` in it takes `--ink` (`--ink-muted` fails on `--surface-hover`).
- The heading in the summary (`h2`, `h3` or `h4`, no class needed) uses the label type one step up (`--font-size-200`), in `--ink`: it names the group. A count or a path goes after it in `eis-mono`.
- A `--line` separates stacked disclosures. To list several, put them as direct children of one `eis-panel`.
- Content goes right after the summary: an `eis-panel__body` for text and fields, or an `eis-table` (its first row drops its top line, the summary line already separates them), then an optional `eis-panel__footer`.
- The styles reach only the disclosure's own summary (`> summary`). A `<details>` inside the content keeps its own style.

##### Metrics (label–value)

```html
<dl class="eis-metrics">
  <div><dt class="eis-label">Open</dt><dd>84</dd><dd>11 streams</dd></div>
  <div class="eis-metrics__cell--accent"><dt class="eis-label">Overdue</dt><dd>06</dd><dd>3 in Platform</dd></div>
</dl>
```

- Always `<dl>`. Each cell is a `<div>` with a `<dt>` (the label, `eis-label`), a `<dd>` (the value) and an optional second `<dd>` (the context line). The CSS sets the context line in mono and `--ink-muted`. Write no class on it.
- The first `<dd>` takes the `metric` type. Write numbers with two digits at least (`06`, not `6`).
- One column per cell: two cells make two columns, four make four. A `--line` separates the cells. Prefer two to four cells. The min height of a cell is `--space-400` × 2.
- Small screens: at ≤760px, two cells stay side by side and four cells go 2 × 2. Other counts stack in one column at ≤640px, with a `--line` between the cells. On a small screen the value drops to `--font-size-600`.
- `eis-metrics__cell--accent` on a cell puts an accent dot before its label. Use it only on the metric that is the exception (overdue, conflict), once per row.
- Put the `<dl>` as a direct child of an `eis-panel`, under its `eis-panel__head`. The cells have their own padding.
- It is the one row of numbers for every scope. The app scope has no metrics component of its own.
- Don't use it for metadata in running text (owner, date, source): use a plain `<dl>`.

##### Breadcrumb and link

```html
<nav class="eis-breadcrumb eis-label" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol><li><a href="/tasks">Tasks</a></li><li aria-current="page">Work</li></ol>
</nav>

<p>Read the <a class="eis-link" href="/foundations">foundations</a> first.</p>
```

- Breadcrumb is `<nav>` + `<ol>`. The current item has `aria-current="page"` and shows in `--accent-ink`.
- Every `<a>` is underlined and turns `--accent-ink` on hover. This is the base style: you get it with no class. Never remove the underline from a link in text.
- `.eis-link` makes a link in running text quieter: `--ink` text with a `--line` underline. On hover the text and the underline turn `--accent-ink`.
- Use `--accent-ink`, not `--accent`, for link text: `--accent` fails contrast as text (3.1:1 on `--surface-panel`).
- Exceptions, set by the component: `.eis-button` links look like buttons, and navigation menus (`.eis-app-nav`, the web header and doc nav) have no underline because the whole item is the target.

##### Lists and avatar

A list in its own box:

```html
<ul class="eis-panel eis-list">
  <li><span class="eis-avatar" aria-hidden="true">AN</span><p>Ana<small class="eis-mono">Release plan</small></p><span class="eis-chip">Waiting</span></li>
</ul>
```

A list inside a panel body, rows to the panel edges:

```html
<div class="eis-panel__body">
  <h3 class="eis-label">Topics</h3>
  <ul class="eis-list eis-bleed">
    <li>
      <p>Checkout<small class="eis-mono">project — New payment flow</small></p>
      <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" checked> Use</label>
    </li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

- Lists are `<ul>`/`<ol class="eis-list">`. A `--line` separates the rows. The first row has no line.
- A row is one line: an optional leading `eis-avatar`, then one `<p>` that takes the free width, then optional trailing items (chips, buttons, a switch). The trailing items stay at the right end and never shrink.
- The `<p>` holds the title. An optional `<small class="eis-mono">` under it holds the description, in muted ink. Long text wraps.
- When the main part of a row is not a `<p>` (for example a `<form>` that edits the row in place), give it `eis-grow`. It then takes the free width like the `<p>`.

A row with a title, a description and a group of options (a topic and the workspaces it applies to):

```html
<ul class="eis-list eis-bleed">
  <li>
    <div class="eis-grow">
      <h6>Atlas</h6>
      <p>project — New billing engine</p>
      <fieldset>
        <legend>Workspaces for Atlas</legend>
        <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-checkbox" type="checkbox" checked> Payments</label>
        <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-checkbox" type="checkbox"> Growth</label>
      </fieldset>
    </div>
    <button class="eis-button eis-button--sm eis-button--danger" type="button">Remove</button>
  </li>
</ul>
```

- Use this form when a row holds more than a title and a description. The main part is a `<div class="eis-grow">` with a heading, then a `<p>`, then a `<fieldset>`. The `<p>` and the `<fieldset>` are optional.
- The heading (`h4`, `h5` or `h6`, no class) looks like the title of the short form. The `<p>` right after it looks like the `<small>` description: mono, muted.
- The `<fieldset>` needs no class. It puts its options (`eis-choice` + `eis-checkbox`) in a row that wraps on narrow screens. Its `<legend>` is hidden on screen, but it MUST name the group for screen readers: write the row title in it (`Workspaces for Atlas`).
- The short form (`<p>` + `<small>`) still works. Use it when the row has only a title and a description.
- Put the box on the list itself (`eis-panel eis-list`) or put the list in an `eis-panel__body`. In a body, add `eis-bleed` so the rows touch the panel edges and do not get the body padding twice.
- Avatar: initials in a circle, `aria-hidden` (the name is in the text). No photos, no colour fills.

##### Divider

```html
<div class="eis-panel__body">
  <ul class="eis-list eis-bleed">…</ul>
  <hr>
  <label class="eis-choice"><input class="eis-switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" checked> Use the shared teams</label>
</div>
```

- `<hr>` is a hairline: one `--border-width-100` line in `--line`, no margin. The gap of the container spaces it.
- Use it to split two parts of the same panel body that have no title. In an `eis-panel__body` it touches the panel edges, like the rows of a list.
- When each part has a title, use `eis-panel__section` (see Panel). The section draws the line. Do not add an `<hr>`.
- Do not use it between panels or between list rows. Panels have their own border and lists draw their own lines.

##### Icons

```html
<i data-lucide="pencil" class="eis-icon"></i>
```

Load at the end of `<body>`, Lucide first:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/lucide@1.66.0/dist/umd/lucide.min.js"></script>
<script src="<src>/shared/js/icons.js"></script>
```

- Load a fixed Lucide version, never `@latest`. A new version can remove or rename an icon. Change the version on purpose and check the pages after the change.
- The set is [Lucide](https://lucide.dev/icons) (ISC licence): line icons with a 2px stroke, the same weight as the system lines. Use the Lucide name in `data-lucide`.
- `eis-icon` is 16px (`--space-200`) and takes the text colour (`currentColor`). Never colour an icon on its own. It follows the button or text it sits in.
- `shared/js/icons.js` calls Lucide on load. Lucide draws only the `<i>` that are on the page at that moment. A page that writes HTML with JavaScript after the load (`innerHTML` from a data file) adds new `<i>`, so the script watches the page and draws them too. A page that writes no HTML with JavaScript does not need that part, and it does no harm.
- Lucide hides the icon from screen readers (`aria-hidden="true"`) and keeps the `class`. Do not write `aria-hidden` on the `<i>`. The text or the `aria-label` of the control carries the meaning.
- Without the network the icon is empty. So an icon never is the only way to know what a control does: the control has text, or `aria-label` plus `title`.
- Inside a button, see "Button with an icon".
- An icon that belongs to an element, not to the content (the marker of a disclosure, the check of a done list, the arrow of the sidebar toggle), is drawn by the CSS. `shared/css/icons.css` holds these Lucide icons as `--icon-<name>` (generated by `scripts/build-icons.py`). A rule uses one as a mask on a pseudo-element, so it takes the text colour and needs no markup and no JavaScript.
- A native `<select>` cannot hold a pseudo-element, so its chevron is a background image. A background image cannot take the text colour. For these icons the script writes a copy with the stroke in a token colour, named `--icon-<name>-<token>` (`--icon-chevron-down-ink`). Add the icon to `INKED` in the script.
- The check of `eis-checkbox` and the chevron of `eis-select` and `eis-multiselect` are Lucide icons (`check`, `chevron-down`). If Lucide has no icon for a need, tell the owner of the system. Do not draw one.
- Never type a character as an icon (`+`, `−`, `→`, `×`, `✓`), in HTML or in CSS `content`.

##### Labels and helpers

- `.eis-label` — label text style (mono, 11, uppercase, `--ink`). For panel titles, table heads, nav section titles, the title of a part of a panel body. It is in `--ink` on every surface: it names what follows, it is not metadata. Measured: 18.9:1 on `--surface-panel`, 17.6:1 on `--surface-canvas`, 13.9:1 on `--surface-head`. Use `eis-mono` for muted metadata.
- `.eis-mono` — mono metadata (12, `--ink-muted`, tabular numbers).
- `.eis-visually-hidden` — hidden on screen, read by screen readers. For captions, legends and labels the design doesn't show.
- `.eis-width-fit`, `.eis-width-100` … `.eis-width-500` — the width of a field, a button or a block: as wide as its content, or the `--width-*` step (128, 192, 256, 360, 480px). Never wider than the container. In a flex row (`eis-app-inline`) the item keeps its width and the others take the rest. In a row of fields (`eis-app-add-bar`, `eis-app-form-row`, `eis-app-filters__fields`) the step is the base and the minimum width of the field: it grows into the free room and wraps when it no longer fits (layout.md §7, "Rows of fields"). `eis-width-fit` in a row of fields keeps the content's width and does not grow. A short select before the field it controls is `<div class="eis-field eis-width-fit">`. Don't write a width in page CSS for this.
- `.eis-grow` — the item takes the free room of its flex row first (it grows three times as fast as the others). In a row of fields it marks the main field: it has no `--width-400` limit, while the other fields stop growing at `--width-400`. Put it on one item per row. With a width helper, the helper sets its base.

##### Not yet in the system

Dialog, popover/menu, tooltip, tabs, toast, pagination. Until they exist, use the native element (`<dialog>`, `popover` attribute, `title`) and style it only with tokens. Propose the element for the system. Do not design it inside a piece.

---

### Layout

Source: https://diegoeis.github.io/eis-ds/docs/manual/layout.md

#### Layout

How to set up a page or piece built with the system.

##### 1. Files to load

A piece is a standalone HTML file. It links one stylesheet:

```html
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link rel="icon" href="<src>/shared/brand/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="<src>/shared/brand/apple-touch-icon.png">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="<src>/<scope>/<scope>.css">
<style>/* this piece's layout only */</style>
```

- `<src>` is the relative path to the `src/` folder at the repository root. From `site/examples/<kind>/` it is `../../../src`.
- `<scope>` is `web` (websites, landing pages, docs) or `app` (dashboards, tools). See §7.
- In a project outside this repository, link `dist/eis-<scope>.min.css` instead: one minified file with the same content and no chained imports. It is generated by `scripts/build-css.py`.
- `<scope>.css` is the only stylesheet to link. It imports `../shared/shared.css` (fonts, shared tokens, base, elements), then the scope tokens and components. Keep `shared/` next to the scope folder. The preconnect lines are optional: they make the fonts load faster.
- `shared.css` imports the fonts, the shared tokens, the base and the elements. The base already sets box-sizing, margins, body type, canvas background and focus. Don't repeat it.
- The piece's `<style>` contains **layout only**: grids, regions, positions, page-specific arrangements. It MUST NOT redefine buttons, chips, fields, tables, panels or any shared element.
- No frameworks or libraries (React, Tailwind, Bootstrap, icon fonts). One exception: Lucide draws the SVG icons (`elements.md`, "Icons"). Load it with `shared/js/icons.js` only when the page has icons.
- The favicon is in `src/shared/brand/`: `favicon.svg` (browser tab) and `apple-touch-icon.png` (180×180, home screen). It is the same in every scope. In a project outside this repository, copy both files next to the page and link the copies. A project with its own brand can use its own favicon.

##### 2. Page skeleton

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>…files above…</head>
<body class="eis-app-shell">
  <header class="eis-app-topbar">…menu button, page name…</header>
  <aside class="eis-app-sidebar" id="sidebar" aria-label="Sidebar">
    <nav class="eis-app-nav" aria-label="Main">…</nav>
  </aside>
  <main class="eis-app-main">
    <header>
      <nav class="eis-breadcrumb eis-label" aria-label="Breadcrumb">…</nav>
      <h1>Page title</h1>
    </header>
    <section class="eis-panel" aria-labelledby="…">…</section>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

A web page (website, landing, docs) uses the web scope instead:

```html
<body>
  <div class="eis-web-sheet">
    <header class="eis-web-wrap eis-web-grid eis-web-header">…</header>
    <main>
      <section class="eis-web-hero" aria-labelledby="hero-h">…</section>
      <section class="eis-web-section" aria-labelledby="…">…</section>
    </main>
    <footer class="eis-web-wrap eis-web-grid eis-web-footer">…</footer>
  </div>
</body>
```

Element roles:

| Region | Element |
|---|---|
| Sidebar / side navigation | `<aside aria-label="…">` — also when it becomes a drawer on mobile |
| Navigation lists | `<nav aria-label="…">` + `<ul>` |
| Page or section heading area | `<header>` (never for the sidebar) |
| Main content | `<main>`, one per page |
| Content blocks | `<section aria-labelledby>` (has a heading) or `<article>` (stands alone) |
| Footer of page, panel or sidebar | `<footer>` |
| Dates and times | `<time datetime="…">` |

- Headings in order, one `<h1>` per page. Panel titles are `h2`/`h3` with the `eis-label` class — the visual size doesn't decide the level.
- Interface text and file names in **English**. Example content is **fictional**: invented first names, invented codes like `PLT-204`. Never use real people, clients or data.

##### 3. Spacing the page

| Where | Space |
|---|---|
| Page padding | `--space-300` desktop, `--space-200` below 1024px |
| Gap between page regions (header, metric row, panel grid) | `--space-300` |
| Gap between panels in a grid | `--space-200` |
| Panel padding, row padding | `--space-200` |
| Inside components | `--space-100` |

Surfaces: page on `--surface-canvas`, content in `--surface-panel` panels. Nothing else. No background grid, no gradients, no shadows.

##### 4. Grids and responsiveness

Every piece MUST work from 360px to wide screens with **no horizontal scroll**, no clipped text and no overlap.

- Fluid first: `grid`, `flex`, `minmax`, `clamp()`. Breakpoints only where the composition breaks.
- Auto grids MUST use `minmax(min(<px>, 100%), 1fr)`:
  ```css
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(250px, 100%), 1fr));
  ```
  A bare `minmax(250px, 1fr)` overflows when the container is narrower than 250px.
- Grid and flex children that contain text: `min-width: 0` (or `minmax(0, 1fr)` columns) so long text wraps instead of pushing the layout.
- Display titles: `font-size: clamp(--font-size-600, 5vw, --font-size-800)`.
- Typical breakpoints so far:
  - 1280px: the side column drops below.
  - 1024px: the sidebar becomes a drawer, opened from the top bar (`eis-app-topbar`).
  - 760px: tables reflow, metrics with two or four cells go in two columns (four make 2 × 2).
  - 420px: toolbar buttons stretch.
- A horizontal nav that can't fit scrolls **inside itself** (`overflow-x: auto` on the nav), never the page.
- Tables: reflow to cards with CSS, or scroll inside a wrapper.

##### 5. Slides and fixed-ratio pieces

- Each slide is a container. Set `container-type: inline-size` and `aspect-ratio: 16/9`.
- Size everything inside in container units (`cqw`), so the slide scales as one object.
- Use the same tokens for colour, line and type families. Sizes in `cqw` are the allowed exception to px tokens.

##### 6. Data visualisation

- Data as a matrix of equal cells (like device keys) or thin bars. No pie charts, no 3D, no gradients.
- Grey ramp for normal values, `--accent` only for the exception (see `tokens-usage.md` §2).
- Every chart has `role="img"` and an `aria-label` that states the numbers.
- Legends are lists (`<ul>`), `aria-hidden` if the `aria-label` already carries the data.

##### 7. Scopes: shared, web and app

eis-ds is several design systems in one. They share the same base and never conflict.

| Folder | Use for | Load | Class prefix | Variable prefix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/shared/` | Every scope | Imported by each scope entry. Optional `shared/js/icons.js` (with Lucide) for icons, `shared/js/multiselect.js` for the multi-select | `eis-` | `--color-`, `--space-`, `--ink`… |
| `src/web/` | Websites, landing pages, marketing pages, documentation | `web/web.css` or `dist/eis-web.min.css`, optional `web/js/lines.js` | `eis-web-` | `--web-` |
| `src/app/` | Dashboards, tools, system screens | `app/app.css` or `dist/eis-app.min.css`, optional `app/js/sidebar.js` | `eis-app-` | `--app-` |

To build a website, copy `src/shared/` and `src/web/`. To build a dashboard, copy `src/shared/` and `src/app/`. More scopes (slides, email, docs) follow the same pattern.

Rules:
- `shared` never depends on a scope. Shared elements (button, chip, fields, table, panel) and, later, icons live there.
- A scope's tokens live under its own group (`web.*`, `app.*`) and MAY reference shared tokens: `"{font.size.800}"`. A colour change in shared reaches every scope.
- A scope MUST NOT reference another scope's tokens, variables or classes.
- Every selector in `<scope>/css/components.css` starts with `.eis-<scope>-`. A scope never styles bare HTML or shared classes on their own. It MAY place a shared element in its own context (`.eis-app-task-table.eis-table`) for layout only.
- Use an `eis-*` class only if eis-ds has it. A class of your own page uses your own prefix, never `eis-`. In this repository, the frame classes of the documentation pages use `doc-`. A `doc-` frame can sit directly in an `eis-panel`, and a panel with a `doc-` class is a frame: `scripts/check-css.py` does not check their panel structure.
- `scripts/build-tokens.py` validates the token rules. `scripts/check-css.py` validates the CSS rules. It also fails when `index.html` or a page in `site/` uses an `eis-*` class that is not in `src/**/*.css`. It does not read `<script>` blocks. Both scripts MUST pass.
- A pattern used on two or more pages goes into the scope CSS. A pattern used on one page only stays in that page's `<style>`.

###### Web components

| Class | What it is |
|---|---|
| `eis-web-docnav` | Top bar of documentation pages |
| `eis-web-page`, `eis-web-intro`, `eis-web-toc` | Documentation page shell, intro with title and facts, table of contents |
| `eis-web-doc` | Documentation section: title column + content column |
| `eis-web-spec`, `eis-web-pair`, `eis-web-scroll` | Specification table, contrast pair sample, horizontal scroll wrapper |
| `eis-web-docfoot` | Footer of documentation pages |
| `eis-web-sheet`, `eis-web-wrap`, `eis-web-grid` | Landing sheet on the canvas (always 32px from the window edge, 24px up to 760px), side padding, 12-column grid |
| `eis-web-header`, `eis-web-brand` | Landing top bar and brand mark |
| `eis-web-hero` (`__index`, `__meta`, `__lead`, `__sub`, `__actions`) | Hero block |
| `eis-web-lines` + `data-eis-web-lines` | Line art drawn by `web/js/lines.js`. Options: `data-seed`, `data-step` |
| `eis-web-section` (`__head`, `__body`) | Landing section. `__head` holds the label, the `h2` and an optional `p`. The label and the title use the left five columns. The `p` goes to the right six columns, level with the bottom of the title. Do not put a class on the `p` and do not move it out of `__head`. Without a `p`, `__head` uses the left five columns and `__body` sits next to it. With a `p`, `__body` goes below it in the right column |
| `eis-web-numbered`, `eis-web-cards`/`eis-web-card`, `eis-web-principles`, `eis-web-steps` | Numbered list, cards with a figure, principles grid, step timeline. A chip at the end of `eis-web-card__body` keeps its own width (for example `Future` on a surface that is not available yet). `eis-web-card__figure` on the card `<figure>` puts one short code (`<span>`) at the bottom left in large mono type. `eis-web-card__figure--accent` fills it with the accent. Use the accent on one card only |
| `eis-web-proof` | Band of proof numbers on a landing (`<dl>`): each cell is a `<div>` with a `<dt class="eis-label">`, the value `<dd>` in `metric` type and a context `<dd>` in muted ink. Cells wrap at 200px or more, with a `--line` above the band and under each cell. No panel. For a row of numbers in a panel, use the shared `eis-metrics` |
| `eis-web-plans`, `eis-web-plan` (`__price`) | Pricing cards. `eis-web-plans` is the grid (cards of 280px or more). Each card is a `<section class="eis-panel eis-web-plan">` with an `eis-panel__body` and an `eis-panel__footer`. The body holds a label, an `h3`, a `<p class="eis-web-plan__price">` (price in `metric` type, period in a `<small>`) and a `<ul>` of features. The footer holds one button. The bodies fill the cards, so the buttons line up. Mark the plan you recommend with one `eis-chip--accent` in its label |
| `eis-web-faq` | Questions and answers on a landing: an `eis-panel` with one `eis-disclosure` per question (the question as `<h3 class="eis-label">` in the `<summary>`). Each answer is a `<p>` in muted ink, 64 characters wide at most, with space under it. Put it on the `eis-web-section__body` |
| `eis-web-code`, `eis-web-cta`, `eis-web-footer`, `eis-web-arrow` | Code block, closing call to action, landing footer, arrow link |

Panel parts: `eis-web-scroll` (around a table) and an `eis-web-spec` table go directly in an `eis-panel`, after its head, in place of an `eis-panel__body` (elements.md, "Panel structure"). Every other web component goes in a body. `scripts/check-css.py` keeps the same list in `PANEL_CONTENT`: change both together.

###### App components

| Class | What it is |
|---|---|
| `eis-app-shell` | On `<body>`: sidebar + main grid. Below 1024px: the top bar, then the main region; the sidebar is a drawer |
| `eis-app-topbar` (`__title`) + `data-eis-app-drawer-toggle` | First in `<body>`, below 1024px only: a bar fixed at the top with the menu button on the left (`eis-button--ghost eis-button--icon`, Lucide `menu`) and the page name on the right. The button opens the sidebar as a drawer. Driven by `app/js/sidebar.js`. See "Mobile drawer" below |
| `eis-app-sidebar` (`__foot`), `eis-app-brand`, `eis-app-nav` (`__section`, `__count`, `__toggle`, `__sub`) | Sidebar, brand, navigation with counts. The sidebar is as tall as the window and scrolls inside when its content is taller; `__foot` stays at its bottom, on the sidebar background. `__foot` takes one `eis-app-nav__section` before the toggle, for links to other apps (the eis-ops plugin pages): a label, then plain links, lined up with the toggle's arrow. Section labels (`eis-label`) in the sidebar, in the nav and in the footer, are `--color-neutral-500`. An item that holds a sub-list is either a link followed by an arrow-only `<button class="eis-app-nav__toggle">` (the link navigates, the arrow opens the list) or a `<button class="eis-app-nav__toggle">` with the item's text (the whole row opens the list). Both take `aria-expanded aria-controls data-eis-app-nav-toggle` and are followed by `<ul class="eis-app-nav__sub">`; `app/js/sidebar.js` opens and closes it and keeps the state. See "Nav sub-list" below |
| `eis-app-sidebar__toggle` + `data-eis-app-sidebar-toggle` | Collapse button at the bottom left of the sidebar, last in `eis-app-sidebar__foot`. Driven by `app/js/sidebar.js`. Collapsed, the sidebar keeps only the button. Above 1024px only. See "Sidebar collapse" below |
| `eis-app-main`, `eis-app-page-head` (`__meta`), `eis-app-toolbar` | Main region (content max `--app-size-main`, in the centre of the free space), page head, action toolbar. See "Page head" below |
| `eis-app-grid` (`--halves`, `--main`), `eis-app-stack` | Panel grids and the side column stack |
| `eis-app-agenda`, `eis-app-cells`, `eis-app-legend`, `eis-app-bar`, `eis-app-pips` | Agenda list, cell matrix, legend, stacked bar, pips |
| `eis-app-task-meta` | A task's fields in one line under its text: `<dl class="eis-app-task-meta">` with one `<div><dt>Source</dt><dd>…</dd></div>` per field (label upper case, value in ink, at most `--space-300` × 5 wide, cut with an ellipsis). Use `—` for an empty value |
| `eis-app-notes` | Dated notes under a task (the sub-items of a markdown task): `<ul class="eis-app-notes">`, each `<li>` a `<time>` (or an empty `<span>`) then a `<div>` with the text. A rule on the left; the date column stacks above the text below 760px; a long note grows with its text and does not scroll. A small icon button (`eis-button--ghost eis-button--icon eis-button--sm`) at the end of a note's `<p>` sits inline, right after the text: use it to delete the note |
| `eis-app-priority` (`--highest`, `--high`, `--medium`, `--low`, `--lowest`) | The priority of a task, on a small chip at the end of the task title, after a no-break space: `…the last word&nbsp;<span class="eis-chip eis-chip--sm eis-app-priority--high">High</span>`. Never on a line of its own. One colour per level, strongest first |
| `eis-app-add-bar` | The form that adds an item, first in a list panel, before its groups: `<form class="eis-app-add-bar">` with `eis-field`s side by side, aligned on their bottom edge, then an `eis-app-inline` with Cancel and Save. The fields are a row of fields (see "Rows of fields" below): give the short ones a width helper and the main one `eis-grow`. An `eis-field__error` takes a row of its own |
| `eis-app-task-table`, `eis-app-task-title`, `eis-app-meta`, `eis-app-due` | A table of tasks, on `<table class="eis-table eis-app-task-table">` (cells aligned to the top; columns in this order: `eis-app-col-idx` (the number), `eis-app-col-check`, the task, then `-src`, `-date`, `-due` or `-act` (one small button); below 760px the number hides and the checkbox takes the first column; rows become cards below 760px), the task title when it is not a `<label>` (`--cancelled`: struck through like a done task, for a cancelled one; `--editable`: a text cursor, for a title a double click edits; chips go in the title line, a state chip before the text and the priority and "New" chips at its end after a no-break space, so a chip wraps with the last word and never alone; in a done or cancelled title the chips are not struck through), task metadata, due dates. To group tasks, put each table in an `eis-disclosure` inside an `eis-panel` (shared element). There is no group component: `eis-disclosure` is the only element that opens and closes |
| `eis-app-topics`, `eis-app-people`, `eis-app-done` | Side lists |
| `eis-app-filters` (`__fields`, `__search`) | Filter bar above a list: `eis-tabs` on the left, labelled fields on the right. The fields are a row of fields (base `--app-size-filter-field`, `__search` `--app-size-filter-search`). When they do not fit next to the tabs on one line, they move as one block to a row of their own and fill it |
| `eis-app-notice` | One status line (`role="status"`), sticky at the top while the user scrolls a long list |
| `eis-app-flash` | The result of one button, right next to it (`role="status"`): "Saved" beside Save. `data-state="ok"` (success ink) fades out by itself once the page adds `data-fade`; `data-state="error"` (danger ink) stays. Empty = hidden. Use it when the result belongs to that button; use `eis-app-notice` for the page |
| `eis-app-code` | A generated file shown as text (JSON, markdown) inside a panel. Scrolls inside itself |
| `eis-app-messages` (`__head`) | Messages grouped by day: one `<section>` per day, a day heading, then one message panel per message |
| `eis-app-message` (`__head`, `__meta`, `__quote`, `__score`, `__bar`, `__notes`, `__notes--accent`, `__sent`, `__state`, `__task`, `--marked`, `--handled`) | One message on an `<article class="eis-panel">`: head strip (`eis-panel__title` with number and sender, chips, then time, source link and app logo on the right), then `eis-panel__body`: the quote as it arrived first, as an `eis-bleed` (square, touches the edges, optional score on its top right, out of the flow), the reply, collapsible notes and `eis-panel__footer` (action buttons, state text at the right end, optional inline form). `--marked`: accent outline. `--handled`: quote in muted ink |
| `eis-app-menu` (`__list`) | A button that opens a small row of choices (`role="menu"`, items `menuitemradio`). The list opens above the row, at the left of the nearest positioned container |
